div.l: [son of Laertes] and king Menelaus son of Atreus
led them, and the father, wise-counseling hero,
and his sons—the message of the Achaeans.
gathered the ranks of the Trojans
and lifting up their hands to the immortal gods
they prayed for release from woes.
Muse, who first began the righteous speeches?
Menelaus, son of Pleisthenes, with enchanting voice
spoke out, taking counsel with the fair-robed Graces:
high-ruling Zeus, who beholds all things,
is not the cause of great griefs to mortals;
rather it lies open in the midst
for all men to find straight Justice, attendant
of pure Good Order and wise Themis:
